verses.1: Judge me, God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation, from a deceitful and wicked man. Deliver me from their hands.
verses.2: For you are my God, my stronghold—why have you abandoned me? Why must I walk in gloom, oppressed by my enemy?
verses.3: Send out your light and your truth; they will lead me and bring me to your holy mountain and to your dwelling places.
verses.4: I will go to the altar of God, to the God who brings joy to my youth. I will praise you with the lyre, O God, my God.
verses.5: Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why do you groan within me? Hope in God, for I will still praise Him, the salvation of my face and my God.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "Why must I walk in gloom" reflects the Hebrew "לָֽמָּה־קֹדֵר אֶתְהַלֵּךְ," where "קֹדֵר" is interpreted as a rare or poetic term for gloom or darkness.
- v. 3: "Send out your light and your truth" uses the imperative form typical in psalms of supplication. "They will lead me and bring me..." reflects the poetic parallelism of the Hebrew.
raw:
[1] Judge me, God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation, from a deceitful and wicked man. Deliver me from their hands.

[2] For you are my God, my stronghold—why have you abandoned me? Why must I walk in gloom, oppressed by my enemy?

[3] Send out your light and your truth; they will lead me and bring me to your holy mountain and to your dwelling places.

[4] I will go to the altar of God, to the God who brings joy to my youth. I will praise you with the lyre, O God, my God.

[5] Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why do you groan within me? Hope in God, for I will still praise Him, the salvation of my face and my God.
